blocks.x: Dataq Nexus's architecture: the planes, the controls and the evidence export — documented the way your auditors will read it.

The Dataq Nexus architecture is three planes and an evidence spine. Modules compose behind one governed API; every decision crossing a plane boundary is logged with the inputs, the policy version and the accountable owner.
In Dataq Nexus architecture, the build decomposes into named pieces, each with an owner and a gate:

items: one governed entry point with SLA guarantees
versioned decision policies with effective-dating and simulation
shadow scoring and incremental traffic shifting
online feature store with point-in-time correctness

blocks.x: The program tracks these without being asked — Dataq Nexus edition:

Runtime dependencies: Databricks Feature Store, Kafka/Flink, Redis, OPA, core-system adapters. Deployment runs inside your security perimeter with customer-managed keys; the evidence export is formatted for the audit formats your team already uses.

Deployment models for Dataq Nexus follow the estate: in-perimeter on customer-managed keys, or in a segregated enclave where the estate cannot host the workload. Either way the control pack, the replay log and the audit export keep the same format, so the second deployment never re-argues the first.
If Dataq Nexus architecture is on your agenda this year, a briefing will tell you in 45 minutes whether this pattern fits your estate.
